questions.question: When driving a tractor-trailer with ABS, what should you do?

options.text: Use extra braking force to activate the ABS.
Brake using less pressure than normal.

questions.explanation: With ABS on a tractor-trailer, brake the same way you would in a vehicle without ABS.

questions.question: If your vehicle breaks down while carrying explosives, how can you warn other drivers?

options.text: By standing on the road and waving your arms.
By keeping the driver's door open.

questions.explanation: When your vehicle breaks down with explosives, use electric lights or reflective triangles to warn other drivers. Do not use flares or other signals that could start a fire.

questions.question: An improperly placarded vehicle can only be moved:

options.text: To make room for other vehicles.
If the trip is shorter than 10 miles.

questions.explanation: A vehicle must have proper placards before it can be driven. An improperly placarded vehicle can only be moved if it is necessary to protect lives or property in an emergency.

questions.question: How often must you check that cargo is properly secured?
questions.explanation: Check cargo securement before you start, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles.

questions.question: Which is NOT a sign of damaged brakes?

options.text: Shoes with oil or grease on them.
Pads free of oil or grease.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pads free of oil or grease.
questions.explanation: Signs of brake problems include cracked drums, shoes or pads with oil or grease on them, and worn-thin shoes. Clean pads without oil or grease are normal and not a problem.

questions.question: When you see a construction worker near the road, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until all construction is finished.

questions.explanation: When driving through work zones, reduce your speed, especially when workers are on or near the road.

questions.question: What is important to know about transporting radioactive materials?

options.text: Radiation will pass through to other packages.
The package should be placed in the cab.
The package should be loaded on its side.
The package should be made of wood.

questions.correctAnswerText: Radiation will pass through to other packages.
questions.explanation: Radiation passes through to nearby packages. The number of radioactive packages loaded together is limited.

questions.question: A pre-trip inspection should:

options.text: Never be done the same way twice.
Always be done in the same order.
Only be done on sunny days.
Be skipped if the vehicle seems to be working well.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be done in the same order.
questions.explanation: Do a pre-trip inspection the same way every time. This helps you remember all the steps and makes sure you do not miss anything.

questions.question: If you feel drowsy while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Keep driving to finish your trip.

questions.explanation: The only real solution for drowsiness is sleep. Caffeine and other drugs may help temporarily, but you will be even more tired when they wear off.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, where should you NOT park?

options.text: For only short periods of time.

questions.explanation: Never park a vehicle with Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, or building. Park only briefly and at least five feet away from the road.

questions.question: If you are unsure whether your vehicle can safely fit under a bridge, what should you do?

options.text: Swerve as you pass under the bridge.

questions.explanation: If you are not sure your vehicle will fit under a bridge, slow down. Find another route if you can.

questions.question: What are portable tanks?

options.text: Cannot be removed from a vehicle.
Are not permanently attached to a vehicle.
Are permanently attached to a vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are not permanently attached to a vehicle.
questions.explanation: Cargo tanks stay on a vehicle all the time. Portable tanks are loose cargo containers that can be removed from a vehicle.

questions.question: If a truck has a trailer brake hand valve, what can it do?

options.text: Stop the vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stop.
questions.explanation: A trailer brake hand valve stops a tractor-trailer from rolling backward when you start moving from a stop.

questions.question: What is true about hydroplaning?

options.text: It only happens at very high speeds.
It can happen at speeds as slow as 30 mph.
It happens most often when tire pressure is too high.
It happens most often when tires have good tread.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can happen at speeds as slow as 30 mph.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is enough water on the road. It is most likely when tire pressure is too low or when tire tread is worn.

questions.question: What should you know about driving a bobtail tractor?

options.text: Bobtails cannot drive as fast as tractors with trailers.
Bobtails are harder to stop than tractors with trailers.
Bobtails are illegal in most states.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bobtails are harder to stop than tractors with trailers.
questions.explanation: A bobtail is a tractor with no trailer attached. Bobtails take longer to stop and are harder to stop than tractors pulling loaded trailers.

questions.question: What must emergency response information from the shipper include?

options.text: How many people should respond to an accident.

questions.explanation: Emergency response information must include basic descriptions and names of the materials, health hazards, fire and explosion risks, safety steps for accidents, how to handle fires, how to handle spills, and first aid steps.

questions.question: How should small hazardous material packages be labeled if they are too small for a full HazMat label?
questions.explanation: If a hazardous material package is too small for a regular label, attach the label to a tag and secure the tag to the package.

questions.question: What should you do with your mirrors when making a tight maneuver?

options.text: Do not use them because they are distracting.
Use them, but not too often.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often when making tight maneuvers.

questions.question: What does the emergency air line do?

options.text: Is controlled by the foot brake.
Is connected to the relay valves.
Supplies air to the trailer air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Supplies air to the trailer air tanks.
questions.explanation: The emergency air line (supply line) has two jobs. It supplies air to trailer air tanks on combination vehicles and controls the emergency brakes.

questions.question: What will you be asked to do during the vehicle inspection test?

options.text: Explain what you would inspect and why.
Estimate the weight of cargo in a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain what you would inspect and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must inspect your vehicle and explain to the examiner what you are checking and why.
